html:
SMTO-UI-0063 — Too many sign-in attempts, so wait a minute

GUID: 62c1f53c-584a-5f33-b64e-a97409a91308
Slug: portal-login-limited
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • SMTO has paused sign-in for about a minute because there were several failed attempts for this account or from this computer. The pause protects the account from password guessing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait at least one full minute without selecting Sign in. During the pause SMTO refuses every sign-in, even with the right password.
  2. Type your username and password carefully, with Caps Lock off, and select Sign in once. Several wrong passwords caused the pause, so a correct next try avoids another one.
  3. If you're not sure of your password, ask your administrator to reset it instead of guessing. More wrong guesses will start the pause again.

What success looks like

  • After the wait, SMTO either opens your workspace or says the username or password is wrong, instead of asking you to wait.

If it still fails

  • If you keep seeing this even after waiting, tell the person who manages SMTO; someone else may be trying to sign in to your account. Select Copy error details to include. Never share your password or browser cookies.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • POST /auth/login returned 429 with Retry-After: 60 because the account store raised LoginLimited: repeated failed attempts within the 60-second window for this client address or username, too many attempts across the installation, or no free password-check slot.

What this means

  • The server temporarily limited sign-in attempts. This reports access to the current request, not the outcome of previous operations.

Why this can happen

  • The server temporarily limited sign-in attempts.

How to diagnose it

  • A later sign-in attempt receives an authentication result.

How to fix it

  • Wait for the 60-second window (Retry-After) to pass before submitting again; attempts are counted per client address and per username, with an installation-wide cap. If it recurs without user error, look for another client or script repeatedly sending wrong credentials for this account or from this address.
  • Wait one minute before trying your credentials again. Avoid repeated submissions while the limit is active.

Retry and execution caution

  • A later sign-in attempt receives an authentication result.

How to verify the fix

  • A later sign-in attempt receives an authentication result.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
